```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

de Witte et al. (2018) refitted the rat morphine plasma, brain
extracellular-fluid (ECF) microdialysis and EEG data of Groenendaal et al.
(2007) to ask whether the delay between morphine concentrations and the
increase in EEG delta-band amplitude is better described by an effect
compartment (EC), by drug-target binding kinetics (TB), or by both (EC-TB).
Seven pharmacodynamic models from the paper are packaged here, each as a
self-contained model that carries the same plasma and brain-ECF layers:

| Model file | Paper model | PD driver | Delay / link | GF120918 acts on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_ecpl1` | ECPL1 (best overall, Table 4) | plasma | transit + effect compartment, sigmoidal Emax | k1e, keo |
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_tbpl4` | TBPL4 (Table 5) | plasma | target binding, linear in occupancy | KD |
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_ectbpl1` | EC-TBPL1 (Table 6) | plasma | effect compartment then target binding | KD |
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_tbecf1` | TBECF1 (Table 7) | brain ECF | target binding, linear in occupancy | KD |
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_deecf1` | DEECF1 (Table 7) | brain ECF | direct sigmoidal Emax | Emax |
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_ececf1` | ECECF1 (Table 7) | brain ECF | effect compartment, sigmoidal Emax | Emax |
| `deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_ieecf1` | IEECF1 (best ECF model, Table 7) | brain ECF | indirect response (stimulated ksyn) | Emax |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_ecpl1"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-018-9593-x> (open access,
  PMC6061075), with Supplementary material 1 (equations, plasma and ECF
  parameter tables, goodness-of-fit plots and VPCs).

```{r models, message = FALSE}
model_names <- paste0(
  "deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_",
  c("ecpl1", "tbpl4", "ectbpl1", "tbecf1", "deecf1", "ececf1", "ieecf1")
)
model_labels <- c("ECPL1", "TBPL4", "EC-TBPL1", "TBECF1", "DEECF1", "ECECF1", "IEECF1")
names(model_labels) <- model_names
uis <- lapply(setNames(model_names, model_names), function(nm) {
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm))
})
```

# Population

```{r population}
str(uis[[1]]$population)
```

Male Wistar rats received a 10-min intravenous infusion of 0 (vehicle), 4, 10
or 40 mg/kg morphine (Table 1). Nine of the 29 rats in the 4 mg/kg group
also received the P-glycoprotein (Pgp) inhibitor GF120918 (elacridar) as a
continuous infusion. Plasma was sampled in 54 animals, brain ECF by
microdialysis in 29 and EEG in 54. The EEG endpoint is the amplitude in the
delta band (0.5-4.5 Hz), recorded every minute and averaged over 3-min
intervals.

The analysis was sequential. The plasma three-compartment model (Supplement
S1, Table S1) was fitted first. Its individual estimates then drove the
brain-ECF model (Table S2), and all individual PK estimates were held fixed
while each EEG model was fitted. The plasma-driven models (ECPL, TBPL,
EC-TBPL) used all EEG animals. The ECF-driven models (Table 7) used the
reduced dataset of animals with ECF data.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The
plasma and brain-ECF layers are identical in all seven files.

```{r source-trace-pk, echo = FALSE}

  "sigma^2 prop (plasma)", "0.079", "Table S1 prints '0.79 (14)'; see Errata",
  "kdiff (1/min)", "0.0025", "Table S2, 'IIV on kdiff, Nmax'",
  "keff (1/min)", "0.020", "Table S2",

```

tibble::tribble(

  "ECPL1", "Table 4: k1e 0.0393, keo 0.0382, k1e-Pgp 0.0565, keo-Pgp 0.016, E0 45.1, Emax 27.9, EC50 1270, NH 1.44, slope -0.024, omega^2 E0 0.111, sigma^2 0.0554", "S1 eqs 10-12; Figure 1",
  "TBPL4", "Table 5: koff 0.009, KD 1570, KD-Pgp 381, Rtot 1 FIX, E0 45.4, Emax 32.9, slope -0.0299, omega^2 E0 0.113, sigma^2 0.0584", "S1 eqs 16-17; Figure 2",
  "EC-TBPL1", "Table 6: koff 0.0275, keo 0.0327, KD 1520, KD-Pgp 296, Rtot 1 FIX, E0 45.0, Emax 31.8, slope -0.0276, omega^2 E0 0.111, sigma^2 0.057", "S1 eqs 13-15 (eq 13 sign corrected); Figure 3",
  "TBECF1", "Table 7: koff 0.0932, KD 283, KD-Pgp 55.9, E0 48.9, Emax 32.7, slope -0.0400, omega^2 E0 0.0668, sigma^2 0.0598; Rtot 1 nM assumed", "Figure 4c with S1 eqs 16-17",
  "DEECF1", "Table 7: E0 48.9, Emax 23.4, Emax-Pgp 41.6, EC50 173, NH 2.3, slope -0.0359, omega^2 E0 0.072, sigma^2 0.0598", "Figure 4a",
  "ECECF1", "Table 7: keo 0.161, E0 49.1, Emax 24.9, Emax-Pgp 43.2, EC50 182, NH 2.02, slope -0.0373, omega^2 E0 0.0696, sigma^2 0.0593", "Figure 4b",
  "IEECF1", "Table 7: kdeg 0.124, E0 49.1, Emax 25.4, Emax-Pgp 43.3, EC50 182, NH 2.07, slope -0.0377, omega^2 E0 0.0961, sigma^2 0.059", "Figure 4d; Table 7 footnote a"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "EEG pharmacodynamic layer, one row per model (units: rate constants 1/min, concentrations nM, EEG uV).")
```

Inter-animal variability is log-normal on every parameter (paper eqs 1-2),
and all residual errors are proportional (eq 3). The tables report omega^2
and sigma^2, so `propSd` is `sqrt(sigma^2)`. A separately estimated
"-Pgp" parameter is encoded as a log-ratio covariate effect,
`exp(lP + e_conmed_elacridar_P * CONMED_ELACRIDAR)`, which reproduces both
tabulated values exactly.

# Virtual cohort and dosing

The model time `t` is experiment time. The linear EEG drift `slope * t` is
anchored at the start of EEG recording, and the morphine infusion starts at
about t = 60 min (the first plasma samples and the rise of the EEG in
Figures S2, S3 and S10 sit there). Doses in mg/kg are converted to nmol per
animal with the free-base molar mass (285.34 g/mol). Body weight is not
reported in de Witte 2018, so weights are drawn uniformly from the 250-350 g
range of the source experiment.

```{r cohort}
mw_morphine <- 285.34 # g/mol, free base
t_dose <- 60 # min, start of the 10-min infusion (read from Figures S2 / S10)
obs_times <- seq(0, 430, by = 3)

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~dose_mgkg, ~CONMED_ELACRIDAR,
  "0 mg/kg", 0, 0L,
  "4 mg/kg", 4, 0L,
  "4 mg/kg + GF120918", 4, 1L,
  "10 mg/kg", 10, 0L,
  "40 mg/kg", 40, 0L
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm))

make_events <- function(n_per_arm, weights = NULL, times = obs_times) {
  subj <- arms |>
    slice(rep(seq_len(n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
    mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
  subj$WT <- if (is.null(weights)) runif(nrow(subj), 0.25, 0.35) else weights
  subj$amt_nmol <- subj$dose_mgkg * subj$WT * 1e6 / mw_morphine
  doses <- subj |>
    filter(dose_mgkg > 0) |>
    transmute(id, arm, CONMED_ELACRIDAR,
      time = t_dose, amt = amt_nmol, rate = amt_nmol / 10,
      evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs <- subj |>
    select(id, arm, CONMED_ELACRIDAR) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  # Three error endpoints (Cc, Cbrain_ecf, eeg): every observation row must
  # nominate one through dvid; all three observables are returned as columns
  # on every row regardless.
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    select(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, dvid, everything()) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180518)
set.seed(20180518)
n_per_arm <- 100
events <- make_events(n_per_arm)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))
```

# Simulation

Each model is simulated twice: a stochastic cohort (100 animals per arm,
inter-animal variability on, residual error off) and a typical-value solve
(`zeroRe()`) at 0.3 kg.

```{r simulate, message = FALSE}
sim_all <- bind_rows(lapply(model_names, function(nm) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(uis[[nm]], events, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(model = model_labels[[nm]])
})) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model_labels))

events_tv <- make_events(1, weights = 0.3, times = seq(0, 430, by = 1))
# zeroRe() solves of several subjects warn that there is no omega; that is
# the intent here, so only that warning is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
tv_solve <- function(ui, ev = events_tv) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
}
tv_all <- bind_rows(lapply(model_names, function(nm) {
  tv_solve(uis[[nm]]) |> mutate(model = model_labels[[nm]])
})) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model_labels))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Plasma and brain-ECF concentrations (Figures S2 and S5)

```{r fig-plasma, fig.cap = "Simulated plasma morphine (median and 5th-95th percentile of individual predictions, ECPL1 cohort). Compare with the left panel of Figure S2 of de Witte 2018: about 10,000 nM at the end of a 4 mg/kg infusion and about 100 nM by 300 min."}
pk_sum <- sim_all |>
  filter(model == "ECPL1", arm != "0 mg/kg", time > t_dose) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    across(c(Cc, Cbrain_ecf), list(
      lo = ~ quantile(.x, 0.05), med = median, hi = ~ quantile(.x, 0.95)
    )),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(pk_sum, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Cc_lo, ymax = Cc_hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cc_med)) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Plasma morphine (nM)")
```

```{r fig-ecf, fig.cap = "Simulated brain-ECF morphine (median and 5th-95th percentile). Compare with Figure S5: individual fits peak at about 100-300 nM after 4 mg/kg and about 1,000-2,000 nM after 40 mg/kg."}
ggplot(pk_sum, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Cbrain_ecf_lo, ymax = Cbrain_ecf_hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cbrain_ecf_med)) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Brain ECF morphine (nM)")
```

## EEG prediction interval for ECPL1 (Figure S10)

```{r fig-vpc, fig.cap = "ECPL1: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the simulated individual EEG amplitude (residual error not added). Replicates the simulated-quantile bands of Figure S10 of de Witte 2018 (baseline median about 45 uV, rising after the infusion starts at about 60 min)."}
sim_all |>
  filter(model == "ECPL1") |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(eeg, 0.05), med = median(eeg), hi = quantile(eeg, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = med)) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "EEG delta amplitude (uV)")
```

## All seven models side by side

The paper's central finding is that the EC, TB and combined models give
nearly the same EEG time courses over the studied doses (Figures S10-S12),
so the delay alone cannot tell the mechanisms apart.

```{r fig-compare, fig.cap = "Typical-value EEG amplitude (0.3 kg rat) for the seven packaged models."}
ggplot(tv_all, aes(time, eeg, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "EEG delta amplitude (uV)", colour = "Model")
```

```{r table-peaks}
tv_all |>
  group_by(model, arm) |>
  summarise(
    eeg_t0 = first(eeg),
    eeg_peak = max(eeg),
    t_peak = time[which.max(eeg)] - t_dose,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(arm != "0 mg/kg") |>
  mutate(across(c(eeg_t0, eeg_peak), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model, "Arm" = arm, "EEG at t = 0 (uV)" = eeg_t0,
    "Peak EEG (uV)" = eeg_peak, "Peak time after dose start (min)" = t_peak
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value EEG peak by model and arm.")
```

# Model checks

Every check below uses deterministic typical-value solves, with no
random effects, so the tolerances can be tight.

```{r checks, message = FALSE}
# 1. Vehicle arm: no drug, so every model must return exactly E0 + slope * t.
placebo <- tv_all |> filter(arm == "0 mg/kg")
placebo_err <- sapply(model_names, function(nm) {
  p <- placebo[placebo$model == model_labels[[nm]], ]
  th <- uis[[nm]]$theta
  max(abs(p$eeg - (exp(th[["le0"]]) + th[["drift"]] * p$time)))
})
placebo_err
stopifnot(all(placebo_err < 1e-6))

# 2. Plasma mass balance: AUC(0-inf) * CL equals the dose.
ev_long <- make_events(1, weights = 0.3, times = seq(0, 6000, by = 1)) |>
  filter(arm == "4 mg/kg")
pk_long <- tv_solve(uis[[1]], ev_long)
auc_inf <- sum(diff(pk_long$time) * (head(pk_long$Cc, -1) + tail(pk_long$Cc, -1)) / 2)
dose_nmol <- ev_long$amt[ev_long$evid == 1]
cl_typ <- exp(uis[[1]]$theta[["lcl"]])
mass_ratio <- auc_inf * cl_typ / dose_nmol
mass_ratio
stopifnot(abs(mass_ratio - 1) < 0.01)

# 3. GF120918 has no retained effect on plasma or brain-ECF disposition.
#    The two solves differ only in adaptive step sizes (the EEG states
#    differ), so the comparison is relative.
gf_pair <- tv_all |>
  filter(model == "ECPL1", arm %in% c("4 mg/kg", "4 mg/kg + GF120918")) |>
  select(arm, time, Cc, Cbrain_ecf) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(Cc, Cbrain_ecf))
rel_gap <- function(a, b) max(abs(a - b)) / max(abs(a))
gf_gap <- c(
  Cc = rel_gap(gf_pair[["Cc_4 mg/kg"]], gf_pair[["Cc_4 mg/kg + GF120918"]]),
  Cbrain_ecf = rel_gap(gf_pair[["Cbrain_ecf_4 mg/kg"]], gf_pair[["Cbrain_ecf_4 mg/kg + GF120918"]])
)
gf_gap
stopifnot(all(gf_gap < 1e-4))

# 4. Target-binding models: with no drug depletion, the EEG depends on
#    occupancy only, so the fixed Rtot value cannot change the prediction.
ui_rtot <- uis[["deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_tbpl4"]] |> rxode2::ini(lrtot = log(0.01))
rtot_diff <- max(abs(tv_solve(ui_rtot)$eeg - tv_solve(uis[["deWitte_2018_morphine_rat_tbpl4"]])$eeg))
rtot_diff
stopifnot(rtot_diff < 1e-3)

# 5. Saturable influx: the dose-normalised brain-ECF AUC falls with dose.
ecf_auc <- tv_all |>
  filter(model == "ECPL1", arm %in% c("4 mg/kg", "40 mg/kg")) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    dose = first(as.numeric(sub(" mg/kg", "", arm))),
    auc_dn = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cbrain_ecf, -1) + tail(Cbrain_ecf, -1)) / 2) / dose
  )
ecf_auc
stopifnot(ecf_auc$auc_dn[ecf_auc$arm == "40 mg/kg"] < ecf_auc$auc_dn[ecf_auc$arm == "4 mg/kg"])
```

The next check compares the typical-value peaks with the ranges the
individual fits span in the supplement figures, read by eye. Plasma peaks
at 5,000-10,000 nM after 4 mg/kg (Figure S2). Brain ECF peaks at about
100-300 nM after 4 mg/kg and 1,000-2,000 nM after 40 mg/kg (Figure S5). The
brain-ECF check is the main test of the borrowed C50.

```{r checks-figures, message = FALSE}
tv_peaks <- tv_all |>
  filter(model == "ECPL1") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(Cc_max = max(Cc), Cbrain_ecf_max = max(Cbrain_ecf), .groups = "drop")
tv_peaks |>
  mutate(across(-arm, ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Typical plasma Cmax (nM)" = Cc_max,
    "Typical brain ECF Cmax (nM)" = Cbrain_ecf_max
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value (0.3 kg) peak concentrations.")
pk4 <- tv_peaks[tv_peaks$arm == "4 mg/kg", ]
pk40 <- tv_peaks[tv_peaks$arm == "40 mg/kg", ]
stopifnot(
  pk4$Cc_max > 3000, pk4$Cc_max < 10000,
  pk4$Cbrain_ecf_max > 100, pk4$Cbrain_ecf_max < 300,
  pk40$Cbrain_ecf_max > 1000, pk40$Cbrain_ecf_max < 2000
)
```

# PKNCA validation

de Witte 2018 reports no NCA, so the plasma NCA below documents the
simulated exposure by dose group. The plasma model is linear, so the
dose-normalised AUC differs between arms only through the randomly drawn
animals.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_all |>
  filter(model == "ECPL1", arm != "0 mg/kg", !is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = t_dose, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
PKNCA::PKNCA.options(progress = FALSE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Cmax (nM)" = cmax, "Tmax (min)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (nM*min)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (min)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated plasma NCA (ECPL1 cohort; Tmax is measured from the start of the 10-min infusion at t = 60 min, on the 3-min observation grid).")

auc_dn <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(arms |> mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |> select(arm, dose_mgkg), by = "arm") |>
  group_by(arm, dose_mgkg) |>
  summarise(auc_dn = median(PPORRES / dose_mgkg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
auc_dn
```

## Sensitivity to the unreported C50

The brain-ECF C50 is not reported anywhere in de Witte 2018 and is fixed to
the Groenendaal 2007 value for the same data (34.8 nM). Plasma
concentrations are far above that value around the peak, so the saturable
influx runs near its maximum there. In a typical-value solve, moving C50
from 3.48 to 348 nM changes the brain-ECF peak by about 7% at 4 mg/kg and
by less than 1% at 40 mg/kg. It does change the late tail after 4 mg/kg, where plasma falls to
about 40 nM by 400 min: the ECF concentration at 400 min is about 116, 78
and 24 nM for C50 = 3.48, 34.8 and 348 nM. C50 does not enter the EEG
predictions of the three plasma-driven models (ECPL1, TBPL4, EC-TBPL1); it
affects the four ECF-driven models through their driver.

```{r fig-c50, message = FALSE, fig.cap = "Typical brain-ECF morphine for C50 = 3.48, 34.8 (packaged) and 348 nM."}
c50_grid <- c(0.1, 1, 10) * 9.92 * 1000 / 285.34
c50_sens <- bind_rows(lapply(c50_grid, function(c50) {
  ui_c <- uis[[1]] |> rxode2::ini(lc50 = log(c50))
  tv_solve(ui_c) |> mutate(C50 = sprintf("%.1f nM", c50))
})) |>
  filter(arm %in% c("4 mg/kg", "40 mg/kg"))

ggplot(c50_sens, aes(time, Cbrain_ecf, colour = C50)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Brain ECF morphine (nM)", colour = "C50")

c50_table <- c50_sens |>
  group_by(arm, C50) |>
  summarise(peak = max(Cbrain_ecf), at_400 = Cbrain_ecf[time == 400], .groups = "drop")
c50_table |>
  mutate(across(c(peak, at_400), ~ round(.x))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "C50" = C50, "Brain ECF peak (nM)" = peak,
    "Brain ECF at 400 min (nM)" = at_400
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical brain-ECF morphine across the C50 grid.")
peak_spread <- c50_table |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(rel = (max(peak) - min(peak)) / max(peak))
peak_spread
stopifnot(all(peak_spread$rel < 0.08))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **C50 of the saturable brain influx is not reported.** Supplement S1 eq 9
  contains C50, but no table, text, figure or supplement gives its value.
  The packaged value is `fixed()` at the Groenendaal 2007 estimate for the
  same rats (Table 3, 9.92 ng/mL = 34.8 nM with the free-base molar mass);
  S1 calls the ECF structure "the original one compartment ECF model", and
  the de Witte estimates of kdiff, keff and Nmax (0.0025 /min, 0.020 /min,
  2.6 nM/min = 0.74 ng/mL/min) are close to Groenendaal's (0.0014 /min,
  0.0195 /min, 0.66 ng/mL/min). This is non-paper provenance; see the C50
  sensitivity figure above. Whether de Witte et al. re-estimated or fixed
  C50 is not stated.
* **Plasma residual variance.** Table S1 prints sigma^2 prop for the
  selected plasma model as "0.79 (14)". It is read as 0.079 (SD 28%): the
  neighbouring columns print 0.0766 and 0.071, and the observed-versus-IPRED
  plot in Figure S2 is far tighter than an 89% proportional SD would allow.
* **EC-TBPL1 effect-compartment sign.** Supplement S1 eq 13 is printed as
  keo * (C_EFF - C1), which diverges from zero initial conditions. It is
  encoded as keo * (C1 - C_EFF), consistent with the Figure 3 caption
  ("distribution rate constant into and out of the effect compartment").
* **EC-TBPL1 koff.** The Discussion quotes koff as 0.275; Table 6 gives
  0.0275 /min, which is used.
* **ECPL1 transit chain as printed.** S1 eqs 10-11 feed the effect
  compartment at k1e and drain it at keo (Figure 1), so the effect-site
  concentration is not plasma-equivalent at steady state unless k1e = keo.
  The equations are encoded as printed.
* **TBECF1 Rtot.** Table 7 has no Rtot row. Rtot = 1 nM fixed is assumed,
  as in all plasma binding models; check 4 above shows the prediction does
  not depend on it.
* **ECF-driven model structures.** The paper gives no equations for the
  ECF-driven models. DEECF1, ECECF1 and IEECF1 are built from Figure 4 and
  the Table 7 parameter list. ECECF1 uses keo for both inflow and outflow of
  the effect compartment (Figure 4b). For IEECF1, Table 7 footnote a
  defines Emax as (ksyn,max - ksyn,0) / kdeg with ksyn,0 = E0 * kdeg, so the
  response pool starts at E0 and its steady state is E0 + Emax * S(C). The
  paper does not say where the linear drift enters the indirect-response
  model; it is added to the output, as in every other model.
* **Time origin.** `slope * t` uses experiment time from the start of EEG
  recording. The morphine infusion start at t = 60 min is read from
  Figures S2, S3 and S10; the paper does not state it.
* **Dose units.** Doses are given in mg/kg and concentrations in nM; the
  salt form is not stated, so the free-base molar mass 285.34 g/mol is used
  for the conversion. Body weight is not reported; 250-350 g (uniform) is
  taken from the source experiment.
* **Sequential estimation.** The PD parameters were estimated with each
  animal's PK held at its individual estimate. The packaged models carry
  the population PK variability of Tables S1 and S2 instead, and treat the
  PK and PD random effects as independent.
* **Plasma versus blood.** de Witte 2018 calls the concentrations plasma
  concentrations; Groenendaal 2007 analysed the same samples as blood.
* **Not packaged.** The non-selected variants in Tables 4-6 (ECPL2-4,
  TBPL1-3 and 5, EC-TBPL2-5), the ECPL1 refit on the reduced dataset in
  Table 7, the alternative plasma and ECF models of Tables S1 and S2, and
  the one-compartment target-binding simulation study of Figures 5-7 and
  Supplements S2-S3 (a theoretical grid over kon and koff with no fitted
  parameters).
* **Literature check (2026-11-25).** The only published correction (doi:
  10.1007/s10928-018-9604-y) changes the copyright line and no model
  content.
